title: Credit Card Input Auto-Formatting in 4-Digit Space-Separated Chunks (Baymard Checkout)
description: According to Baymard Institute research (2025–2026), typing errors in unformatted 16-digit credit card fields are a primary driver of checkout abandonment. Credit card inputs must accept spaces on input/paste and automatically format digits into 4-digit chunks (`4444 4444 4444 4444`, or `4-6-5` for Amex) using `inputmode="numeric"` and `autocomplete="cc-number"`.
playwright_check_snippet: const ccInputs = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('input[autocomplete="cc-number"], input[name*="card" i], input[id*="card" i]')); if (ccInputs.length === 0) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; const valid = ccInputs.every(el => { const maxLen = el.maxLength; return (maxLen === -1 || maxLen >= 19) && el.type !== 'number'; }); return valid ? 'APPLIED_PASS' : 'VIOLATED_FAIL';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If a payment or credit card form is visible on the screenshot, check whether the card number input displays a 4-digit chunked format mask (e.g., '0000 0000 0000 0000') and card network icon. If no payment form is present, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Use `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="cc-number" maxlength="23" placeholder="0000 0000 0000 0000" />` (never `type="number"`) and format live input with `val.replace(/\D/g, '').replace(/(\d{4})(?=\d)/g, '$1 ')`.

title: Stored Payment 'Fake Editing Flow' Without Forcing Card Deletion First
description: Because PCI DSS rules often restrict direct mutation of tokenized cards, many sites force users to delete a saved card before adding updated details. Per Baymard benchmarks, sites must provide a 'Fake Editing Flow': an explicit 'Edit' button opens a pre-populated form (expiration date, name, billing address, or replacement number) that mints a new payment token on save and silently deletes the old token in the background.
playwright_check_snippet: const savedCards = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[class*="saved-card" i], [data-testid*="payment-method" i]')); if (savedCards.length === 0) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; const hasEdit = savedCards.every(card => /edit/i.test(card.textContent || '')); return hasEdit ? 'APPLIED_PASS' : 'VIOLATED_FAIL';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If stored payment methods or saved credit cards are shown, verify that each saved card provides an explicit 'Edit' action alongside 'Remove', rather than only showing a 'Delete' button. If no saved payment methods exist on the page, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Render an `'Edit'` button on every saved payment card. When the user submits updated details, create a new payment token via your gateway and subsequently call `DELETE /payment-methods/:oldTokenId`.

title: Avoid Horizontal Tabs for Core Product Page (PDP) Content Sections
description: Baymard eye-tracking studies show that 27% of users overlook critical product details (Description, Specifications, Customer Reviews, Q&A, Shipping) when hidden inside horizontal tabs. Core PDP sections must be laid out in a vertically stacked hierarchy with a sticky jump-link navigation bar or mobile accordions.
playwright_check_snippet: const isPdp = !!document.querySelector('[itemtype*="Product"], [data-page-type="product"], button[name*="add-to-cart" i]'); if (!isPdp) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; const tabPanelsHidden = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('[role="tabpanel"][hidden], .tab-pane:not(.active)')); return tabPanelsHidden.length === 0 ? 'APPLIED_PASS' : 'VIOLATED_FAIL';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If the page is an e-commerce Product Detail Page (PDP), check how Product Description, Specifications, and Customer Reviews are laid out. Fail if they are hidden behind horizontal tabs where only one tab's content is visible at a time; pass if they are vertically stacked or accessible via jump-links. If not a PDP, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Replace horizontal `<Tabs>` on Product Detail Pages with vertically stacked `<section id='specs'>` and `<section id='reviews'>` blocks paired with a sticky anchor jump-bar (`position: sticky; top: 64px;`).

title: Always Signpost Hidden Thumbnails in Product Image Galleries
description: Product image galleries must never clip the thumbnail strip cleanly along the edge of a whole thumbnail without indicating that additional photos exist. Always signpost additional media via a `+N photos` badge, a partially cut-off next thumbnail (`overflow-peek` of 30–40%), or a persistent `1 / 8` counter.
playwright_check_snippet: const galleries = document.querySelectorAll('[class*="gallery" i], [class*="carousel" i], [data-testid*="gallery" i]'); if (galleries.length === 0) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If an image gallery or media carousel is present on the page, check whether additional hidden images are clearly signposted via a '+N more' badge, a partially cut-off next thumbnail, or a '1/N' counter. If no image gallery exists, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Overlay a `+4 more` badge on the final visible thumbnail in desktop strips, or set `grid-auto-columns: 82%` on mobile carousels so the leading edge of the next image peeks into view.

title: Applied Filters Overview Bar & Support for 8 Core Search Query Types
description: In product catalogs and search views, active filters must not remain buried inside collapsed sidebar accordions: an 'Applied Filters' summary bar must appear directly above results with removable filter chips (`×`) and a 'Clear All' action. Search inputs must support all 8 core Baymard query types: 1) Exact Product, 2) Product Type, 3) Symptom/Problem, 4) Compatibility, 5) Feature/Attribute, 6) Price/Sale, 7) Brand, and 8) Typo/Synonym queries.
playwright_check_snippet: const hasSearchOrFilter = document.querySelector('input[type="search"], [role="search"], [class*="filter" i]'); if (!hasSearchOrFilter) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If the page contains product listings, data tables with filters, or a search bar, verify that active filters are summarized in a clear horizontal chip bar above the results with a 'Clear all' option, and the search input clearly communicates what users can search for. If no search or filtering UI exists, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Render `<AppliedFiltersBar filters={activeFilters} onRemove={...} onClearAll={...} />` above the results grid, and configure hybrid search indexing to parse attributes, compatibility models, price modifiers, and typo-tolerant synonyms.

title: My Account Dropdown (7 Core Paths With Hierarchy) & On-Site Order Tracking (6 Details + Cancellation Requested State)
description: Per Baymard Account Self-Service standards: 1) The 'My Account' menu must expose all 7 core paths (Orders, Returns, Addresses, Payment Methods, Account Settings, Saved Lists/Wishlist, Sign Out) with visual hierarchy separating primary and secondary actions. 2) Order status views must integrate all 6 tracking details directly on-site (without forcing carrier redirects: status, estimated delivery date, checkpoint history, address, tracking number, package items) and support a `'Cancellation Requested'` intermediate state when instant warehouse cancellation is unavailable.
playwright_check_snippet: const accountTrigger = document.querySelector('[href*="account"], [href*="profile"], [href*="orders"], [aria-label*="account" i], [aria-label*="profile" i]'); if (!accountTrigger) return 'DOES_NOT_APPLY'; return 'APPLIED_PASS';
vision_prompt_heuristic: If an Account menu, user profile dashboard, or Order Tracking view is visible on the page, check whether the 7 core self-service paths (Orders, Returns, Addresses, Payments, Settings, Lists, Sign Out) are structured with clear visual hierarchy, and whether order tracking shows full on-site progress and a 'Cancel / Cancellation Requested' workflow. If no account or order UI is present, return DOES_NOT_APPLY.
remediation_guide: Structure the Account dropdown with all 7 core self-service paths (highlighting 'Orders' and 'Returns' at the top), ingest carrier webhooks to render all 6 tracking details natively on-site, and add `CANCELLATION_REQUESTED` to your order state machine.
